nl.title: User xxxx has used up –% of their bandwidth and –% of his/her allocated disk space
nl.excerpt: Betekenis van “used up X% bandwidth/disk” mails en wat je moet doen.
nl.bodyHtml:
DirectAdmin stuurt usage-warnings vóór harde limieten. Handel vóór 100%.

Voorbereiding

  • Welke resource: disk of bandwidth

Stappen

  1. Open usage-grafieken in DA
  2. Ruim disk of reduceer traffic
  3. Plan upgrade als trend structureel is
  4. Bevestig dat cron/backups niet exploderen

Controleren

  • Percentage daalt of stabiliseert

Tip: Negeer 80–90% warnings niet in piekmaanden.

Let op: Reseller: check welke user de piek veroorzaakt.

Kom je er na deze stappen niet uit? Open een ticket bij TripleZero iT via het klantenpanel. Vermeld hostname, DirectAdmin-gebruikersnaam (geen wachtwoord), domein en wat je al probeerde.

Gerelateerd: bandwidth; disk-usage-da.

User xxxx has used up –% or their bandwidth and –% or his/her allocated disk space is solved via DirectAdmin. Below are concrete steps for user, xxxx, used, including verification afterwards.

Preparation

  • Access to DirectAdmin
  • Focus of this article: user, xxxx, used
  • Note of the current setting/status

Steps

  1. Go to DirectAdmin. Keep this article (“User xxxx has used up –% or their bandwidth and –% or his/her allocated disk space”) beside you so you only make the intended change.
  2. Select the correct domain/user account in DirectAdmin.
  3. Open the module that fits user (Email, DNS, File Manager, SSL, Cron Jobs, MySQL or Installatron).
  4. Note the current status, then apply only what “User xxxx has used up –% or their bandwidth and –% or his/her allocated disk space” requires around xxxx.
  5. Save and test outside DirectAdmin (browser, webmail, DNS lookup or cron log).
  6. Document what you changed around user, xxxx, used (old → new value) for support.

Verify

  • Result for user, xxxx, used matches “User xxxx has used up –% or their bandwidth and –% or his/her allocated disk space”
  • No regression on a critical flow beside user xxxx used
  • External test or second browser/network confirms the result

Tip: Work in small steps: get user, xxxx, used right first, then optional extras.

Note: Do not blindly change production without a backup if user, xxxx, used touches login, DNS, mail or payments.

Still stuck? Open a ticket with TripleZero iT via the client panel. Include your domain name, what you already tried, and any exact error messages (text or screenshot).
